zh: 本书不是一部研究性或考证性的著作，而是一部阐释与概念化的著作，更确切地说，是重新概念化的著作。因为随着苏联共产主义的消亡，十月革命以来四分之三个世纪里产生的大量分析，在很大程度上已经过时。重新思考苏联经验的意义——以及我们此前自以为了解的有关其意义的一切——的时刻已经到来。
en: This book is not a work of research or erudition, but of interpretation and conceptualization, or more exactly of reconceptualization. For with the demise of Soviet Communism, the great body of analysis generated during the three-quarters of a century since the October Revolution has become in large part superannuated. The time has arrived for a major rethinking of the meaning of the Soviet experience—and of all that we had previously thought we understood about its meaning.

zh: 苏联历史如今终于可以完全用过去时来书写。直到1991年，苏联的存在仍是我们日常生活的一部分，而且是全世界政治生活的一块主要试金石。原因之一在于，苏联的抱负在二十世纪政治中是独一无二的。大多数主要国家都声称自己对世界其余部分具有非同寻常的意义——美国自视为自由民主的“山巅之城”，英国自视为“无法无天的劣等民族”的导师，法国自视为向较不开化民族传播“文明使命”（

）的承担者。然而苏联走得更远，它声称自己是良善社会的唯一典范、人类事务的黄金标准，以及历史终结处的完美政体；而且它在全世界找到了千百万相信这些说辞的人。因此，这是一个无人能够回避的挑战。因此，对于任何人都可以说：“告诉我他怎么看待苏联，我就能告诉你他怎么看待自己的社会。”这个命题也可以轻易反过来：“告诉我他的国内政治，我就能告诉你他对苏联的感知。”于是，我们对苏联现象的一切评论，同时都是对我们自身的隐含评论，因此我们在追溯苏联记录时的客观性正处于最低点。如今，我们第一次从苏联存在对日常生活的压力下解放出来，应当有可能把客观性提升一大截。
en: Soviet history may now at last be written entirely in the past tense. Until 1991, the Soviet presence was a daily part of our lives, and indeed a major touchstone of political life throughout the world. One reason was that the Soviet Union had pretensions that were unique in twentieth-century politics. Most major nations make claims to have exceptional significance for the rest of the planet—the United States as the “city on a hill” of liberal democracy, Britain as the mentor to “lesser breeds without the law,” and France as the bearer of a

to less enlightened nations. The Soviet Union, however, went beyond this and claimed to be the sole model of the good society, the gold standard of human affairs, and the perfect polity at the end of history; and it found millions throughout the world to believe in these pretensions. It was thus a challenge that no one could refuse to meet. One could therefore say of anyone: “Tell me what he thinks about the Soviet Union, and I will tell you what he thinks about his own society.” And the proposition could just as easily be reversed: “Tell me his domestic politics, and I will tell you his perception of the Soviet Union.” Thus all of our commentaries on the Soviet phenomenon were also implicitly commentaries on ourselves, and hence our objectivity was at its lowest point in tracing the Soviet record. Now, for the first time, we arc liberated from the pressure of the Soviet presence in our daily lives, and it should be possible to raise the level of objectivity a great notch.

zh: 但这一变化首先不会通过积累新的经验知识来实现。随着旧苏联档案的开放，新的事实当然会大量涌现。然而，过去的证据从来不足以改变对一个问题或事件的概念化；这种改变来自我们当下视角的改变。因此，无论多少研究都无法判定法国大革命是否是一场资产阶级革命，或俄国革命是否是一场无产阶级革命；这类问题的解决，取决于当下的政治关切是否使它们成为相关的问题。就法国而言，正如弗朗索瓦·傅勒（François Furet）所论，大革命之后的两百年间，它始终是法国政治中一道活的裂痕，其遗产把左派与右派、社会主义者与自由主义者分隔开来，而1917年之后，各方都把它视为十月的序幕。

因此，法国大革命只有在1970年代苏联神话褪色、国内社会主义前景的激情随之枯竭之后，才算“结束”。于是，大革命是否具有资产阶级性质的问题，在催生了堆积如山的专著之后，悄然消散，不再引导研究。俄国革命虽然尚未“结束”——至少未达到这种程度——围绕它的激情也远未消退，但它在1991年之后呈现出了新的面貌。因此，无论档案中会涌现什么材料，随着我们逐步把苏联的过去与我们自身不断变化的当下剥离开来，它的概念化都将自动改变。
en: But in the first instance this change will not come about through the accumulation of new empirical knowledge. New facts will of course emerge—and in abundance—as a result of the opening of the old Soviet archives. But the evidence of the past is never enough to change the conceptualization of a problem or an event; such a change comes from a change of our perspective in the present. Thus no amount of research can decide whether the French Revolution was a bourgeois revolution, or the Russian Revolution a proletarian one; the resolution of such matters depends on whether or not present political concerns make such problems relevant issues. In the French case, as Francois Furet has argued, for two hundred years after the event the French Revolution remained a living divide in French politics, its heritage separating Left from Right, and socialists from liberals, with each viewing it after 1917 as the prelude to October.

The French Revolution was therefore “over” only in the 1970s, when the Soviet myth faded, draining the passion from the prospect of socialism at home. Hence the issue of the Revolution’s bourgeois character, after generating mountains of monographs, simply faded away and ceased to orient research. Though the Russian Revolution is not yet “over,” at least not to this extent, and the passion surrounding it has far from abated, it assumed a new visage after 1991. Its conceptualization, therefore, will automatically change, whatever materials come out of the archives, as we progressively disentangle the Soviet past from our own changing present.

zh: 然而，当前对俄国革命的重新思考将与法国的情况大不相同。这不是因为十月成为俄国社会内部的一道分界线——1917年之后俄国政治本身便不复存在——而是因为它分裂了国际社会以及国际社会所有成员的国内政治。因此，苏联历史的一个反常之处在于，大部分相关的解释性文献不是俄文，而是西方语言，尤其是英文。原因当然在于，在前苏联，历史写作同其他一切事物一样，被政权“国有化”了。正如第五、七章所述，这一过程在1920年代以波克罗夫斯基的方式零散开始，到1938年在斯大林的官方《简明教程》中达到顶点；那部正典虽在细节上有所修订，其主要轮廓却一直延续到改革时期。这一情形把解释问题的真正争论负担主要留给了外国学者。
en: Yet the present rethinking of the Russian Revolution will be quite different from that of the French case. This is so not because October became a divide within Russian society—Russian politics simply ceased after 1917—but because it divided the international community and the domestic politics of all its members. Thus one of the anomalies of Soviet history is that most of the relevant interpretative literature is not in Russian but in Western languages, and in particular in English. The reason, of course, is that in the former Soviet union historical writing, like everything else, was “nationalized” by the regime. As explained in chapters 5 and 7, this process began in ad hoc fashion with Pokrovskii in the 1920s and culminated in Stalin’s official
in 1938; that canon, though amended in detail, lasted in its main outlines down to
. This circumstance left the burden of genuine debate on issues of interpretation largely to foreign scholars.

zh: 此外，既然苏联政权已经崩溃，俄罗斯的历史学术——如同废墟中的其他一切——必须从头重建。这又引出一个反常之处：在这一重建任务中，俄罗斯学者如今正转向西方文献，以寻求理解自身历史的指引。例如，在苏联解体后第一部——也是迄今唯一一部——从起源到当下的俄国通史中，苏联时期占主导地位的学术参考是西方著作，甚至在革命前时期这类参考也频频出现。
下文注释中也会出现同样的失衡。本书的大多数参考是外国著作，而它所推进的重新概念化在很大程度上是对西方史学的批判。
en: Moreover, now that the Soviet regime has collapsed, Russian historical scholarship, like everything else in the resulting rubble, must be rebuilt

. And this leads to a further anomaly: in this task of reconstruction, Russian scholars are now turning to the Western literature for guidance in understanding their own history. For example, in the first—and so far the only—post-Soviet history of Russia from the beginnings to the present, the preponderance of scholarly reference is to Western works for the Soviet period, and such references are frequent even for the prerevolutionary period.

The same imbalance will appear in the citations below. Most of the references in this book are to foreign works, and the reconceptualization it advances is largely a critique of the Western historiography.

zh: 再者，由于重点在于概念化而非覆盖范围，详尽的参考书目和注释并无必要。因此，每章的注释首先提及主要的相关二手著作，为希望查阅原始资料和主要评论的读者提供指引。在此之后，才提供更精确的注释，仅用于标明正文中较重要的具体论点。
en: Furthermore, since the emphasis is on conceptualization, not coverage, extensive bibliography and annotation are unnecessary. Accordingly, the notes for each chapter begin with mention of the principal relevant secondary works as guidance to readers who wish to refer to the sources and principal commentaries. Following this, more precise annotations are provided only to reference the more important specific points in the text.
